convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom indicator (Ergodic_Ticks_Volume_OSMA) which is not a built-in MT5 indicator, plus external .mqh libraries (TradeAlgorithms.mqh, SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) for trading logic and smoothing algorithms

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars needed for indicator warmup
TimeShiftSec - timeframe duration in seconds
derived_values.used_by: UpSignalTime/DnSignalTime calculation for position open timing

other_exits: Opposite signal closes existing position: short signal closes long (BuyPosClose=true), long signal closes short (SellPosClose=true)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum controls sizing: LOT=fixed lots, BALANCE=MM fraction of balance, FREEMARGIN=MM fraction of free margin, LOSSFREEMARGIN=MM fraction of free margin minus loss, LOSSBALANCE=MM fraction of balance minus loss

custom_logic_notes: The OSMA indicator produces values where Ind[1]<Ind[2] means OSMA is rising (bullish) and Ind[1]>Ind[2] means OSMA is falling (bearish). The actual entry condition is more nuanced: for long entry, Ind[1]<Ind[2] (OSMA rising) AND Ind[0]>=Ind[1] (current bar OSMA >= previous bar OSMA, confirming upward momentum). For short entry, Ind[1]>Ind[2] (OSMA falling) AND Ind[0]<=Ind[1] (confirming downward momentum). SignalBar=1 means signals are read from the previous completed bar (not current forming bar). When SignalBar=0, signals are evaluated on every tick without new-bar guard. The UpSignalTime/DnSignalTime is set to last bar date + timeframe seconds, used by BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen for trade timing. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose are toggle inputs that enable/disable each direction independently.
python_conversion_notes: The custom Ergodic_Ticks_Volume_OSMA indicator must be reimplemented in Python. It uses 7 smoothing passes with configurable methods (SMA/EMA/SMMA/LWMA/JJMA/JurX/ParMA/T3/VIDYA/AMA) from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh - each of these smoothing algorithms (especially JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) needs a Python equivalent. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose which handle margin-based position sizing, stop placement, and order execution - these must be reimplemented with full MarginMode logic. SignalBar parameter allows using bar[1] (completed) or bar[0] (forming) for signal evaluation, which changes whether the strategy is on-bar-close or intrabar. The OSMA calculation chain involves multiple cascading smoothings making exact numerical replication critical for backtest fidelity.
